title: What is Pathways? Single-controller training for large models
summary: Pathways is a single-controller distributed training system designed to coordinate large-scale model training across multiple accelerator groups by representing computations as a global dataflow graph. Unlike traditional SPMD models like DDP and FSDP that rely on synchronous collectives, Pathways uses asynchronous dispatch and a central scheduler to maximize hardware utilization and prevent deadlocks in complex workloads. By decoupling model definition from physical hardware via virtual devices, developers can efficiently scale complex training architectures and seamlessly handle dynamic workloads like reinforcement learning post-training.

title: Moving your VPS to a new provider without downtime
summary:
Every migration horror story has the same middle part: someone changed DNS first and then started copying. Downtime during a move is almost never about the copy being slow. It's about doing the steps in the wrong order.

Here's the order that works, whether you're leaving another provider or moving between two of our plans.

1. Two days before: lower the TTL

Find the DNS records you'll change (usually A, AAAA and any CNAME pointing at them) and drop their TTL to 300 seconds. Then wait at least as long as the old TTL was. A record with a TTL of a day means some resolvers will keep serving the old address for a day after you change it, and nothing you do on the server can speed that up.

This is the step people skip, and it's the one that turns a five-minute switch into a day of half the users seeing the old server.
